- BcDefaultDigestProvider took the output length of an id-shake128-len or id-shake256-len digest identifier from its parameter without any bound, so a CMS SignedData naming one with a length near 2^31 bits made a verifier on the BC lightweight digest path allocate about 256 MB per digest before any signature was checked, and several signers naming distinct lengths multiplied this. An absent, malformed or out of range parameter also escaped as an unchecked NullPointerException, NegativeArraySizeException or ArithmeticException. The length must now be present, positive, a whole number of bytes and at most 4096 bits, and anything else raises an OperatorCreationException, which CMS reports as a CMSException. The JCA path did not allocate, but an absent parameter there also escaped as a NullPointerException and now gives a NoSuchAlgorithmException.

- The GOST R 34.10-94, GOST R 34.10-2001 and GOST R 34.10-2012 Signature implementations read r and s from fixed offsets and ignored the length of the signature, so a valid signature with any bytes appended still verified. Anyone holding a signed certificate, CRL, OCSP response, request or CMS message could produce other encodings of it that verified, and carry arbitrary unsigned data in the signature value. A signature now verifies only if it is exactly 64 bytes, or 128 for GOST R 34.10-2012 with a 512 bit key, as RFC 4491 and RFC 9215 require, and a truncated one now returns false rather than throwing a SignatureException.

- ISO9796d2PSSSigner copied the message it recovered from a signature over the message passed to update() before comparing the two, so the comparison only checked the length and a signature verified against any other message of the same length that differed only in the part recoverable from the signature. For a message short enough to be recovered in full this was any message of the same length. The message passed in is now compared with the recovered one. The class is only reachable through the lightweight API.

+- X931Signer, ISO9796d2Signer and ISO9796d2PSSSigner did not reset on several failing exits of verifySignature(), such as a signature the RSA engine rejected or one with the wrong trailer, and left the message fed so far in place for the next verification on the same object, which then treated it as a prefix of its own input. Given a signature over a message A || B, a failed verification of A followed by a verification of B with the genuine signature on the same object accepted B, and a bad signature caused the next valid one to be rejected. This applied equally to a reused Signature object for the *WITHRSA/X9.31 and *WITHRSA/ISO9796-2 algorithms. Every failing exit now resets the signer. The ISO 9796-2 Signature implementations also now report a signature whose trailer names a different digest as a SignatureException rather than letting an IllegalStateException escape.
